title: Quick to hear (James 1:19–27)
hookLine: swift to hear, slow to speak; pure religion visits orphans and widows
carry: swift to hear, slow to speak

cards: You're telling a friend something that matters. Halfway through, you can see it: they've stopped listening. Their eyes have that look.
They're loading their reply. The second you take a breath, out it comes, about them. It's easy to end up on either side of that.
James has three short rules for it. Then he holds up a mirror, and finally gives his own definition of what religion is for. It fits in one sentence.

teach.h: FAST EARS, SLOW MOUTH, SLOWER TEMPER.
teach.b: In the King James Bible: "Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath." Fast ears. Slow mouth.
Slower temper. The order matters: if you're quick to hear, you're less likely to need the other two. Anger, James says, doesn't produce the kind of goodness God wants.
Then he turns from listening to people to listening to God's word, and pushes one step further.
"But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves." Hearing is not the finish line.

teach.h: THE FORGOTTEN FACE IN THE MIRROR.
teach.b: His picture: someone looks at their face in a mirror, sees it plainly, walks away, and "straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was." Spinach in your teeth. Hair sticking up.
And you walk off and forget. That's hearing without doing. You saw it, and nothing changed.

Then his definition: "Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world." Not a building. Not a feeling.

teach.h: SWIFT TO HEAR, SLOW TO SPEAK.
teach.b: Two things. Show up for the people with no one to protect them, and keep yourself clean. Care outward, integrity inward.
The word for religion here means outward worship, the practice people could see. Put plainly: if you want to see someone's religion, watch where they go on a Tuesday afternoon.

how: Some churches name James 1:27 as the reason for their visiting ministries, food pantries and foster-care support.

o: people who act on what they hear, not just listen
people who keep every ritual rule exactly
people who do good so others will praise them

games.q: what's inside James 1:19–27 — tap the pairs.

s: James defines pure religion as having the right feelings
he defines it as visiting orphans and widows and keeping unspotted.
in James's picture, the man in the mirror forgets his own face
he walks away and "straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was."
James says hearing God's word is enough
"be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only."

games.q: you've just looked in the mirror and seen something wrong. what does James say the hearer who doesn't act is like?
o: walk off and forget what they saw.
games.why: he "straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was." that, says James, is hearing without doing.

practice: For a minute, just listen to the room: a fan, traffic, a bird, your own breathing, the farthest sound and the nearest.
Notice how often your mind wants to comment, to name or judge what it hears, and let the comments go and keep listening. If you pray, you can ask for quick ears.

wordCard.voice: Doers. James's word for those who don't just hear but act: be doers of the word, not hearers only, or you deceive yourselves.

orig.note: Greek: religion as outward worship, the practice others can see. James gives it a practical definition.

carryVoice: Your line: swift to hear, slow to speak. Doers, not hearers only. That's day six hundred seventy-one.
